Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

balancesample 0.1.0

  • First CRAN release.

  • balanced_vfold_cv(), balanced_initial_split(), and balanced_initial_validation_split() make v-fold cross-validation folds, training/testing splits, and training/validation/testing splits that are balanced on several variables at once. The three sets of a three-way split are balanced in one pass. Columns in exact are stratified exactly: each combination of their levels is a stratum, and its count in each set is its share of that set’s actual size, rounded up or down. group keeps the rows of a group in the same set; then the proportions and the exact counts are numbers of groups, and exact columns must be constant within each group. If more than half of the exact strata are missing from at least one set, you get a warning. balance takes numeric, logical, character, factor, Date, POSIXct, and difftime columns. Selected columns must not have missing values; the vignette shows how to balance on a filled copy of a column instead. Printed splits and folds show the method and the columns.

  • Four balancing methods: "anticlust" (k-plus anticlustering, the default), "twinning" (data twinning; needs the twinning package), "rerandomize" (rerandomization on the Mahalanobis imbalance), and "interaction" (random stratification on crossed quantile bins, as a baseline). ?balanced_vfold_cv describes each one and its options.

  • With method = "twinning", only some proportions are allowed (for example, 2 / 3 but not 0.67), and small strata are split at random. See ?balanced_initial_split and ?balanced_initial_validation_split.

  • balance_check() reports standardized mean differences and the energy distance of balanced splits and of rsample’s own splits and resamples. For objects that don’t store balance or exact columns, such as those from rsample::vfold_cv(), name the columns to check. A three-way split is checked as the validation set and the testing set, each against the training set. With variance_ratio = TRUE, it also reports the variance ratio of each numeric variable. summary() gives one row per split, with its largest absolute SMD and its energy distance. autoplot() plots the result with ggplot2.

  • Balanced folds work with tune::fit_resamples() and tune::tune_grid(), and balanced splits with tune::last_fit(). To tune on the validation set of a balanced three-way split, pass it to rsample::validation_set() first. To tune on balanced folds, attach balancesample with library(): rsample finds the function that made the folds by its name (tidymodels/rsample#619).

  • With tune 2.0.0 or later, a postprocessor that must be trained (for example, a tailor calibration) needs an inner split of the analysis set.

    • For balanced folds and a balanced training/testing split, the inner split uses the outer split’s method and columns. If it can’t be made (for example, if there are too few rows or groups), you get a warning and an empty calibration set, as in rsample.
    • Through rsample::validation_set(), rsample makes the inner split at random, so it is not balanced and can split groups (tidymodels/rsample#620).
    • tune::last_fit() can’t train such a postprocessor on any three-way split (tidymodels/tune#1213).
